factual_methodology.summary: Verified historical and 2026 source records for RAND, academic books, DOJ, ESET, Carnegie, NSA, ENISA, Anthropic, Google GTIG, NCSC, NATO, MITRE, NIST and ICRC; observed, alleged and forecast matters separated.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Substantive independent conflict-system research on cyberwarfare, espionage, industry, international law and AI, including competing scholarly theses and falsifiable horizons.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three equivalent analytic tables, two number-matched charts, one causal flow, and one geographic map in each language.

research_depth.summary: 16 aligned sections covering history, theoretical debate, Ukraine, state actors, AI empirical data, agent security, economics, law, physical continuity, geopolitics and scenarios.

evidence_traceability.summary: 27 same URLs from reputable primary, research and official sources across both languages; platform observational sample scope, historic dates and institutional interpretations annotated.

counterfactual_review.summary: Four falsifiable scenarios; counterevidence includes Ukrainian wartime resilience, limited strategic military decisiveness and risk of AI agent evaluation error.

contrary_evidence: Carnegie research on wartime Ukraine finds visible military impact of cyber operations less decisive than many predictions, despite technically significant intrusions and civilian losses.
Real AI-enabled intrusions and agent errors do not demonstrate universal autonomous geopolitical campaign capabilities; platform-specific observational samples cannot estimate global prevalence.
Recovery, offline controls and trusted partnerships can limit civilian and physical impact even where advanced malware has reached operational environments.
limitations: Historical state attribution varies by source and standard of proof; official charges are presented as official allegations, not definitive proof for every incident.
Anthropic's 832-account sample is selected from one provider; changes in internal risk classifications are not global cybercrime statistics.
Long-run cyber and AI scenarios are conditional, lack empirically defensible exact probabilities and must not be read as technology timelines.
The literature and incident record are unevenly observable because many intelligence operations remain classified and successful defense may not generate public evidence.
notes: Internal source-review and structural bilingual QA with 27 reference URLs, parallel charts and explicit differentiation of forensic observations, official attribution and conditional futures; not external academic peer review.
